title: Training Register Demo - DPIA Extraction Fixture

sections.heading: S1 - Context and data subjects
paragraphs: Synthetic draft for UC3-DOC-01. SME approval is pending. No enterprise approval, legal basis or production compliance is asserted.

Training Register Demo (SYN-TRN-001) registers employees for training and tracks course completion. Data subjects are fictional employees enrolled as learners. All records and contacts are fabricated.

facts.quote: Data subjects are fictional employees enrolled as learners.

sections.heading: S2 - Personal-data categories and fields
paragraphs: Employee identification data: employeeId identifies an employee's enrolment; employeeName identifies the learner. Contact data: workEmail records the learner's work contact.

Learning data: courseCode identifies the training course; completionStatus tracks training progress linked to the employee. Both are personal information in an employee-linked enrolment, although neither identifies a person in isolation.
Record identification data: id is an application-generated UUID associated with an employee on newly created records only; seed records have no id.

The synthetic business contact ownerEmail (training.owner@example.test) belongs to application metadata, not learner enrolment records. No passwords, national IDs, IP addresses, authentication tokens, health data or financial data are stored in enrolment records.

sections.heading: S3 - Processing purposes
paragraphs: Purpose P1: register employees for training. employeeId and employeeName associate an enrolment with the learner; workEmail records the learner's work contact; courseCode selects the training course.
Purpose P2: track course completion. completionStatus records enrolled or completed progress against the employee and course. The generated id distinguishes newly created enrolment records.
The application does not send emails, perform marketing, profile employees, or make automated decisions. No consent workflow is implemented.

sections.heading: S4 - Collection, use and sharing
paragraphs: Collection: POST /api/enrolments accepts employeeId, employeeName, workEmail, courseCode and completionStatus from a local HTTP client. The application generates id; clients cannot submit additional fields.
Use: the Node.js service validates input, adds the enrolment to its in-memory array and returns the created record. GET /api/enrolments returns records to any local client without authentication.

Sharing: the local tester is the only intended API recipient, but access is not enforced by identity. No external service integration or email delivery is implemented. Publishing the repository exposes its synthetic seed data and documents according to GitHub repository visibility.

sections.heading: S5 - Storage and retention
paragraphs: Two synthetic seed enrolments persist in fixtures/application.json on the local machine. Runtime enrolments are stored only in Node.js process memory on that machine and are lost on restart; the seed file remains unchanged until manually removed.

No database, cloud deployment, backup, cross-border transfer or automated retention/deletion mechanism is implemented. The service binds to loopback (127.0.0.1) and uses cleartext HTTP. There is no authentication, authorization, audit trail or application encryption-at-rest mechanism. Use synthetic data only.

sections.heading: S7 - Privacy statement requirement
paragraphs: Control TC-PD-03: A privacy statement shall be publicly available and easily accessible to users. The Training Register Demo homepage shall provide a clearly identifiable privacy statement link before users submit employee enrolment data. Users shall be able to open and read the statement without authentication or other access restrictions.

The statement shall describe the personal data collected, the training registration and completion-tracking purposes, intended recipients, storage and retention, and a privacy contact. This is a required control, not an assertion that the supplied frontend implements it. This DPIA is an assessment document, not a substitute for the user-facing statement.

The local registration homepage is served at GET / and submits the five declared client fields to POST /api/enrolments. Code review must compare the supplied homepage and its browser script against this requirement. Repository inspection alone cannot establish deployed accessibility or exclude a statement supplied outside this repository; live verification remains outstanding.
